name: Sun Pengsheng
current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu Nhwa Pharmaceutical Co. (SZSE: 002262), 7th board
profile: Sun Pengsheng (b. 1958) is chairman and one of four co-controlling shareholders (acting in concert) of Jiangsu Nhwa Pharmaceutical, a Xuzhou-based maker of central nervous system drugs. He rose through Xuzhou state pharma factories and has led the Nhwa group since 1996; in April 2026 he bought 200,000 more Nhwa shares.
interesting_fact: He holds about 4.9% of Nhwa directly, and with three partners in a contractual acting-in-concert pact controls roughly 48% of the company directly and via Xuzhou Nhwa Investment.
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1976 as a factory worker at Xuzhou No. 2 Pharmaceutical Factory, then from 1980 rose from technician to director at Xuzhou No. 3 Pharmaceutical Factory; he was once named one of Xuzhou's 'Top Ten Outstanding Youths' and is a CEIBS EMBA.
notes: Company general email published on the corporate site; also Jiangsu provincial People's Congress deputy. Route via company board secretary office.

name: Xing Chengnan
current_role: Shareholder of Hunan Xiangjia Animal Husbandry Co. (SZSE: 002982); no executive role found
profile: Xing Chengnan is a shareholder of Hunan Xiangjia Animal Husbandry (chilled poultry/livestock, Shenzhen-listed since 2020), part of the controlling family alongside actual controller and vice-chairman Xing Weimin, with whom she shares the Hurun listing. Filings show she holds about 2.8 million shares and has delegated her voting rights to Xing Weimin.
interesting_fact: Xiangjia is jointly controlled by Yu Ziwen and Xing Weimin through an acting-in-concert pact, renewed on 28 April 2025 for another five years.
notes: Passive family shareholder (filings describe her as daughter of controller Xing Weimin); no public profile or contacts found. Any outreach should go via Xiangjia's board secretary office or to Xing Weimin/Yu Ziwen.

name: Wang Muqing
current_role: Founder and former chairman of China ZhengTong Auto Services (HKEX: 1728); no current role confirmed
profile: Wang Muqing founded China ZhengTong Auto Services, a luxury-car dealership group (Wuhan-based, HK-listed) and served as its chairman until September 2021, when Wang Mingcheng took over after state-owned Xiamen C&D/ITG interests moved in. Xiamen ITG later took majority, then over 90%, control (2025).
interesting_fact: He stepped down as ZhengTong chairman effective 9 September 2021 after more than two decades building the dealership group; the company has since been taken over by Xiamen state capital.
notes: Low public profile; no longer runs ZhengTong. Current activities and contacts not found. Hurun/Forbes listings date to 2019-2020.

name: Hu Liping
current_role: Former director, vice president and board secretary of Inner Mongolia Yili Industrial Group (600887); current role not confirmed
profile: Hu Liping (b. 1970, Mongolian ethnicity) is a finance executive who spent his career at dairy giant Yili, serving as executive director and board secretary from 2005 and also chairing Yili Finance Co. His wealth comes from roughly 79 million Yili shares built up via the 2006 share reform, equity incentives and stock dividends. He resigned as board secretary in December 2018.
interesting_fact: At end-2017 he held 79.3 million Yili shares (about 1.31%, the 8th-largest holder), worth nearly RMB 2bn at the time he resigned in Dec 2018.
deep_cut_fact: A finance specialist by training, he started out as finance supervisor at a Yili mineral-water subsidiary, then ran the group's settlement centre and was assistant to the president before becoming board secretary.
notes: Has kept a low profile since leaving Yili's board-secretary post in 2018; no public contacts found.

name: Fan Jinsong
current_role: Founder, chairman and actual controller, Anhui Korrun Co. (SZSE ChiNext: 300577)
profile: Fan Jinsong founded Korrun in 2005 after a decade-plus in IT and manufacturing management, including at Lenovo. Korrun is a bag and luggage ODM/OEM maker that also owns consumer brands '90fen' (90FUN) and Guildford; it listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext at end-2016. He remains actual controller per the company's 2026 interim report.
interesting_fact: Korrun runs two businesses: contract manufacturing of bags for global brands, and its own consumer luggage brands 90FUN and Guildford.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding a luggage company he was a tech person: he studied microelectronics at Hefei University of Technology and worked at Lenovo Group, later earning an EMBA at Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.
notes: IR/board-secretary contact email published in Korrun's 2026 interim report summary. Best route is via the board secretary's office.

name: Wu Zhensheng
current_role: Deceased (April 2019); was chairman of Royalcover (Luokafu) home textiles and co-founder of Baoxiniao Group
profile: Wu Zhensheng, co-founder of menswear group Baoxiniao and chairman of Royalcover home textiles, died on 9 April 2019 aged 54 after a traffic accident en route to Shanghai Hongqiao Airport, per Hangzhou News.
notes: Deceased 9 Apr 2019 (source: https://hznews.hangzhou.com.cn/shehui/content/2019-04/12/content_7176056_0.htm). Not a podcast candidate.

name: Luo Aihua
current_role: Chairman of Shenzhen Huachao Investment Development Co. (per Sina profile, dated); former chairman/president of Shenzhen Kondarl (Group)
profile: Likely the Luo Aihua (b. 1960, Guangdong) who chaired Shenzhen Huachao Investment Development, the investment vehicle behind Shenzhen Kondarl (Group), which she also chaired. Trained in architecture, she worked in construction and design firms in Wuhan and Shenzhen before turning to investment. Current activities not found.
deep_cut_fact: A graduate of Wuhan Urban Construction Institute, she once taught building/architecture at Wuhan Workers' University and later headed building projects for Shenzhen design and construction firms.
notes: Match to Hurun 'Hua Chao' entry is by company name only; co-holder Lu Weimin not verified. Source profile is old (c. 2004). Press coverage 2012-2013 involved a legal dispute at Kondarl; treat as sensitive and verify before any outreach.

name: Larry Xiangdong Chen
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Gaotu Techedu Inc. (NYSE: GOTU; formerly GSX Techedu)
profile: Larry Xiangdong Chen founded GSX Techedu (now Gaotu) in 2014 after years at New Oriental, where he was executive president from 2010 to 2014; Gaotu listed on the NYSE in 2019. He holds a PhD in economics from Renmin University. Gaotu, an online education company, reported 30.7% YoY revenue growth in Q3 2025 under his leadership.
interesting_fact: Chen was briefly a billionaire during the 2020 online-education boom before China's 2021 private-tutoring crackdown cut his fortune sharply.
deep_cut_fact: Before New Oriental and Gaotu, he was a schoolteacher in a remote Chinese village.
notes: Active public CEO who comments on every earnings release; IR and its US PR agency (Piacente) are the published routes.

name: Zhang Gengsheng
profile: Listed on the Hurun China list (2021) with Lin Lan for a SaaS company named 'Chase Science'. Searches did not identify the company's Chinese name or confirm this person's role.
notes: Could not identify; Chinese company name for 'Chase Science' needed (check Hurun 2021 list original). Unrelated namesake: a Hebei Normal University math professor.

name: Wu Yueshi
current_role: Former chairman of Yuan Longping High-tech Agriculture (000998); current role not confirmed (Longping's chairman as of July 2026 is Liu Zhiyong)
profile: Wu Yueshi was chairman of Yuan Longping High-tech Agriculture, the Hunan-based hybrid rice and field-crop seed company founded in 1999, and a member of the CPPCC National Committee. His wealth stems from his stake in the company. His current activities are not documented in sources found.
interesting_fact: As a CPPCC National Committee member he argued in a 2014 article that China lacked an enterprise-led, commercialisation-oriented innovation system and that 'organisational design is the key, and incentives for innovative talent are the core'.
notes: Appears to have left Longping High-tech leadership; no current contacts found. Hurun listings 2010-2018.

name: Qian Gaofa
current_role: Chairman, Ningbo Gaofa Automotive Control System Co. (SSE: 603788) (chairman since June 2011; 2023-2026 board term; post-July 2026 status not confirmed)
profile: Qian Gaofa founded the Ningbo company that became Gaofa Automotive Control System in 1999; it makes automotive control cables and shift/pedal systems and listed in Shanghai. He ran Ningbo Gaofa Auto Cable as executive director and GM from 2000 to 2011, then became chairman of the listed company; since 2023 he also heads its new-energy subsidiary.
interesting_fact: Gaofa is a family-run founder company: Qian Gaofa (about 4.9%), and Qian Guoyao and Qian Guonian (about 4.4% each) are the top three shareholders, with Qian Guonian serving as general manager.
deep_cut_fact: Still active in his seventies: in December 2023 he took on the additional post of executive director and GM of Gaofa's new-energy subsidiary (高发新能源), after heading its electronics unit since 2021.
notes: Born c. 1949 (aged 74 in 2023 AR). Contacts are the company's published IR email/site from the 2023 annual report.

name: Lord Zac Goldsmith
current_role: Member of the House of Lords (Lord Goldsmith of Richmond Park, Conservative life peer since Jan 2020)
profile: Zac Goldsmith (b. 1975), son of financier Sir James Goldsmith, is an environmentalist politician whose wealth is largely inherited. He edited The Ecologist (1998-2007), was MP for Richmond Park (2010-16, 2017-19) and a UK environment/climate minister (2019-2023) before resigning in June 2023 over government 'apathy' on the environment; he remains active in the Lords on nature and conservation.
interesting_fact: He resigned his own Commons seat in 2016 in protest at approval of Heathrow's third runway, then stood (and lost) as an independent in the resulting by-election.
deep_cut_fact: Long before politics he was a green philanthropist: he funded the Organic Targets Bill campaign in 1999 and won the 2003 Beacon Prize as Young Philanthropist of the Year; he started at The Ecologist in 1997 as reviews editor under his uncle Edward Goldsmith.

public_contacts.value: holmember@parliament.uk (generic House of Lords members' office address)

notes: Listed jointly with his mother Lady Annabel Goldsmith (Sunday Times). Very public and reachable; energy/climate angle is strong (former Minister for Energy, Climate and Environment).

name: Xu Haiming
current_role: Vice Chairman and President, Zhongshan Broad-Ocean Motor Co. (SZSE: 002249); vice chairman, China Micro-Motor and Component Industry Association
profile: Xu Haiming (b. 1963) has run Zhongshan Broad-Ocean Motor since joining as general manager in 2001; he is vice chairman and president and holds about 140 million shares. Broad-Ocean makes building-ventilation and appliance motors, EV powertrain systems, vehicle starters/alternators and hydrogen fuel-cell components.
interesting_fact: Broad-Ocean, a micro-motor maker, pushed into energy transition tech: it acquired Shanghai Edrive for EV drive systems and took a stake in Canada's Ballard to enter hydrogen fuel cells.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in 1982 at the Wuhan Railway Sub-bureau; in 1992 he became GM of Guangzhou Xiandao Technology Engineering before joining Broad-Ocean in 2001.
notes: Good energy/EV/hydrogen angle for the podcast. Nominated for the 7th board in April 2025.

name: Vernon Hill
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Metro Bank (UK) and Commerce Bancorp (US); no current executive role confirmed (left Republic Bank in 2022)
profile: Vernon W. Hill II (b. 1945) is an American banker who founded Commerce Bank in New Jersey in 1973, grew it to about 470 branches and saw it sold to TD for $8.5bn in 2007, then co-founded Metro Bank, the first new UK high-street bank in over 100 years (2010), chairing it until 2019. He has also chaired pet insurer Fetch (Petplan US) and wrote 'Fans Not Customers' (2012).
interesting_fact: Forbes put him in its 2007 '20-20-20 Club' alongside Warren Buffett and Larry Ellison: CEOs with 20+ year tenures delivering 20%+ annual shareholder returns (Commerce compounded 23% a year).
deep_cut_fact: After Wharton he founded a real estate firm finding sites for McDonald's, which meant driving Ray Kroc on scouting trips; he credits McDonald's for his retail-style 'stores not branches' banking model. He also co-founded Galloway National Golf Club near Atlantic City (Tom Fazio design).
notes: Listed with wife Shirley Hill (InterArch founder). Big veterinary philanthropist (Hill Family Foundation; $10m Vernon and Shirley Hill Pavilion at Penn Vet). No published personal contact found; route via Hill Family Foundation or his publisher Profile Books.

name: Li Meng
current_role: Founder and Chairman, InMyShow / Tianxiaxiu Digital Technology (Group) Co. (SSE: 600556)
profile: Li Meng founded InMyShow (IMS, 天下秀), an influencer-marketing platform that connects brands with social-media creators. After a 2010 Series A from Sina and a SoftBank-linked fund, the company went public via a backdoor listing completed in 2020, billed as the A-share market's 'first influencer-economy stock'. He remains chairman and the person in charge per the 2025 interim report.
interesting_fact: He calls the US$4m Series A from Sina and SoftBank Saif in 2010 the round that 'decided life or death' for the company after early cash-flow trouble.
deep_cut_fact: His view on founders: 'Entrepreneurial passion is not a momentary feeling but a long process of exploration' (创业激情不是一瞬间的感受，而是一个漫长的探索过程), from a 2021 interview.
notes: Active public founder in the creator economy. Sina is a long-time partner/shareholder. Route via IR email.

name: Ari Bousbib
current_role: Chairman and CEO, IQVIA Holdings (NYSE: IQV)
profile: Ari Bousbib has led IQVIA as chairman and CEO since the October 2016 merger of Quintiles and IMS Health, having run IMS Health from 2010. Before that he spent 14 years at United Technologies, rising to CEO of Otis Elevator (2002) and president of UTC Commercial Companies (2008); earlier he was a Booz Allen Hamilton partner. His wealth is largely IQVIA equity.
interesting_fact: At UTC he ran Otis, Carrier, UTC Fire & Security and UTC Power simultaneously: $36bn in annual revenue and 150,000 employees worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 the US President appointed him to the President's Commission on White House Fellowships; he has also sat on The Home Depot's board since 2007 and on Harvard Medical School's Health Care Policy Advisory Council.
notes: Wealth figure is from SEC insider holdings. IQVIA Investor Day scheduled 1 Dec 2026. Utilities/energy link: he once oversaw UTC Power (fuel cells).

name: Li Xiaoxuan
current_role: Founder and Chairman, China New Higher Education Group (HKEX: 2001); CPPCC National Committee member
profile: Li Xiaoxuan founded China New Higher Education Group, a Beijing-headquartered, Hong Kong-listed operator of private universities and colleges, and chairs its board. He is a member of the CPPCC National Committee and vice chair of the China Democratic National Construction Association's Yunnan committee, and campaigns on vocational and higher-education policy.
interesting_fact: At the 2026 national 'Two Sessions' he proposed loosening China's college-to-bachelor's ('zhuanshengben') upgrade rules: removing graduation-year barriers and reserving places for past vocational graduates in skill-shortage industries.
deep_cut_fact: He has said 'Education is entering a buyer's market; private educators must recognise change, respond scientifically and actively seek change' (2023 interview).
notes: IR email from a 2021 HKEX filing (2020 annual report); company website xingaojiao.com was not reachable during research, so verify it is still current.
